result.title: GraphRAGProv: GraphRAG Meets How-Provenance
result.summary: GraphRAG systems often use knowledge graphs to retrieve relevant context for an LLM that produces the final answer. That makes answers more inscrutable and therefore less appealing for domains where transparency is paramount. We present GraphRAGProv, an architecture that executes SPARQL queries over source-grounded RDF graphs to compute answers and their how-provenance polynomials. These polynomials record which statement occurrences were used and how they were combined. Because each occurrence is linked to its source text, users can follow these links to check whether the extracted statements reflect the text and whether the query combines them to answer the question. Querying thereby becomes a way to inspect and evaluate the text-to-graph transformation. Our interactive demo examines 400 cases from two multi-hop QA benchmarks, revealing extraction and query errors even when the final answer is correct.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 GraphRAGProv，在带来源标注的 RDF 图上执行 SPARQL 查询并计算答案的 how-provenance 多项式，记录使用了哪些语句出现及其组合方式，并在两个多跳 QA 基准的 400 个案例中展示抽取与查询错误。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「记录哪些证据被使用、如何组合」的 how-provenance 形式化，可能为 LVR 中的证据筛选与贡献分配提供可核查的追溯线索；但该工作无视觉输入与 latent 状态，迁移需较多改造。
